issues.quote: It has run badly for ten years.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no information about how the watch runs. The only watch readings are the 8:40 reading at nine and the readings at 10:15, 10:18, 10:21 and 10:32 "by my watch".
issues.misreading: "Run badly" with no rate given, read alongside the uncle's remark about what was wrong with the watch, could lead a solver to assume a fixed, known error (about twenty minutes slow) and correct every reading by that amount. That changes every clock time in the puzzle, and the sheet does not support it.

issues.quote: Four years on one watch, and he meant it to strike the first minute of the new century.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for the repeater's making and no date for it to strike.
issues.misreading: A solver could read "four years" as a hint about how long the repeater took or how long it has run, and "the first minute of the new century" as a date-setting clue. Neither is a clock reading or event time in the sheet.

issues.quote: I had brandy, I will admit that, more than I should have.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about drinking or the witness's state of mind.
issues.misreading: A solver might take this as a hint that the witness's time-reading or his account of events is unreliable, which the sheet does not state.
